subTopicTitle: Rajya Sabha or The Council of States

syllabusMapping.prelims: Indian Polity and Governance - Constitution, Political System, Panchayati Raj, Public Policy, Rights Issues, etc.
syllabusMapping.mains: GS Paper II - Parliament and State Legislatures—structure, functioning, conduct of business, powers & privileges and issues arising out of these.

prelimsCapsule.coreConceptSummary: The Rajya Sabha (Council of States) is the upper house of India's bicameral Parliament, designed to protect the federal equilibrium by representing the states and union territories. Unlike the Lok Sabha, it is a permanent body not subject to dissolution, with one-third of its members retiring every second year.
highYieldFacts: Fact 1: Maximum strength is fixed at 250 (238 representing states and UTs, 12 nominated by the President), with current actual strength at 245.
Fact 2: Article 80 of the Constitution lays down the composition and method of allocation of seats based on population (Schedule IV).
Fact 3: The Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Article 64 and Article 89).
Fact 4: Special powers exclusive to Rajya Sabha include Article 249 (legislating on State List subjects) and Article 312 (creation of All-India Services).
Fact 5: Nominated members are drawn from persons having special knowledge or practical experience in literature, science, art, and social service.
trapsAndElimination: Trap 1: The Vice-President is not a member of the House; hence, they cannot vote in the first instance, only exercising a casting vote in the case of a tie.
Trap 2: Nominated members of the Rajya Sabha CAN vote in the election of the Vice-President, but they CANNOT vote in the election of the President of India.

mainsFramework.inDepthTheoryHtml:
Evolution and Constitutional Intent

The architects of the Indian Constitution envisioned the Rajya Sabha not merely as a 'second chamber' for revising legislation passed by the Lok Sabha, but as a vital federal balancing wheel. Operating on the principle of asymmetric federalism, seats are allocated to states in the Fourth Schedule based roughly on population, ensuring that smaller states are not entirely overshadowed by demographic giants. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar famously remarked that a second chamber can act as a cooling chamber, delaying hasty legislation born of populist passions.

Contemporary Institutional Dynamics

In recent years, the functional role of the Rajya Sabha has evolved significantly. With coalition eras receding and single-party majorities frequently dominating the Lok Sabha, the Rajya Sabha has emerged as a crucial site of deliberative democracy. However, questions regarding its efficacy often arise. Controversies surrounding the use of Money Bills (Article 110) to bypass Rajya Sabha scrutiny—such as the Aadhaar Act and tribunal-related amendments—have sparked intense legal and constitutional debates regarding bicameral integrity.

Federal Representation and Nominations

The nomination process under Article 80(3) has brought domain experts, scientists, jurists, and cultural icons into the legislative fold. Yet, the lowering of domicile requirements through the removal of the 'domicile' stipulation in state elections to the Rajya Sabha (amendment of Section 3 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950) has transformed it from a true 'Council of States' into a national arena for political rehabilitation, occasionally undermining local federal representation.

dimensions.constitutional_or_legal: Interplay between Article 110 (Money Bills) and Rajya Sabha powers; special federal provisions under Articles 249 and 312.
dimensions.socio_economic: Representation of marginalized sections and domain experts through presidential nominations; socio-economic oversight via departmental standing committees.
dimensions.administrative_governance: Role of Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committees (DRSCs) administered by the Rajya Sabha Secretariat in scrutinizing budgetary allocations and administrative accountability.
dimensions.international_or_comparative: Comparison with the US Senate (where every state gets equal representation) or the UK House of Lords (hereditary/appointed peerage limitations).

landmarkJudgmentsOrReports: Aadhaar Judgment (K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India, 2018) - examined the passage of legislation as Money Bills to bypass Rajya Sabha.
Rajya Sabha Rules Committee and Secretariat Reforms - emphasis on strengthening DRSCs.
National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution (NCRWC, 2002) recommendations on Rajya Sabha's federal role.

prelims.question: Consider the following statements: 1. Pursuant to the report of H.N. Sanyal Committee, the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971 was passed. 2. The Constitution of India empowers the Supreme Court and the High Courts to punish for contempt of themselves. 3. The Constitution of India defines Civil Contempt and Criminal Contempt. 4. In India, the Parliament is vested with the powers to make laws on Contempt of Courts. Which of the statements given above are correct?
prelims.explanation: Statement 3 is incorrect because the Constitution does not define civil and criminal contempt; the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971 defines them. (Note: Representative UPSC format for parliamentary/legislative domain expertise).

mains.question: Discuss the institutional role of the Rajya Sabha as a federal chamber and examine the challenges confronting its legislative efficacy in recent times.

modelMainsQA.question: Examine the unique constitutional position of the Rajya Sabha in India's parliamentary democracy. How far does it act as an effective federal balancing chamber and a house of second revision? (150 Words, 10 Marks)

approach.intro: Define Rajya Sabha under Article 80 and state its dual constitutional purpose: representing states' interests and providing sober legislative review.
approach.body: Analyze its role as a federal chamber (Articles 249, 312, Schedule IV) and as a revisionary chamber. Highlight contemporary challenges like the circumvention of its authority via Money Bills and disruptions.
approach.conclusion: Conclude by emphasizing that a vibrant Rajya Sabha is indispensable for cooperative federalism and constitutional morality under Vision 2047.

modelMainsQA.modelAnswerHtml:
The Rajya Sabha (Council of States), established under Article 80 of the Constitution, is the federal upper house of the Indian Parliament. Designed as a permanent body, it embodies the federal principle by representing the constituent units of the Indian Union rather than the population directly.


Federal Balancing Wheel and Special Powers:

  • Exclusive Federal Safeguards: Under Article 249, it can empower Parliament to legislate on State List matters in the national interest. Under Article 312, it holds the exclusive right to recommend the creation of new All-India Services.
  • State Representation: Seats are allocated based on population (Fourth Schedule), protecting smaller states from majoritarian dominance.

House of Second Revision and Deliberation:

  • Acting as a 'cooling chamber', it scrutinizes populist or hurried legislation passed by the Lok Sabha through expert debate and Department-related Standing Committees.

Contemporary Challenges:

  • Bypassing Scrutiny: The contentious practice of passing crucial reforms (e.g., Aadhaar Act, tribunal restructuring) as Money Bills under Article 110 has periodically undermined the Rajya Sabha’s legislative authority.
  • Erosion of Federal Link: The removal of the domicile requirement for candidates has occasionally converted it into a arena for political management rather than genuine local representation.

Way Forward: To uphold cooperative federalism, the sanctity of legislative procedures must be protected, ensuring the Rajya Sabha fulfills its foundational mandate as an independent deliberative forum and guardian of India's federal fabric.

practiceMCQs.question: Consider the following statements regarding the special powers of the Rajya Sabha under the Constitution of India: 1. It can authorize the Parliament to make laws on a subject enumerated in the State List. 2. It can authorize the Parliament to create new All-India Services common to both the Centre and the States. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceMCQs.explanation: Statement 1 corresponds to Article 249 (requiring a two-thirds majority of members present and voting). Statement 2 corresponds to Article 312 (requiring a similar two-thirds majority). Both are exclusive constitutional prerogatives of the Rajya Sabha.

practiceMCQs.question: Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding the election and composition of the Rajya Sabha? 1. The representatives of states are elected by the elected members of state legislative assemblies using proportional representation via single transferable vote. 2. Nominated members of the Rajya Sabha are barred from voting in the election of the Vice-President of India.
practiceMCQs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct as state representatives are elected by MLAs using proportional representation by means of single transferable vote. Statement 2 is incorrect because nominated members DO vote in the election of the Vice-President (unlike presidential elections where they are excluded).
